title: OBD-II Drive Cycle Not Complete (P1000-v3)
shortDescription: OBD-II monitors have not finished a full readiness drive cycle yet. Stored as P1000-v3.
fullDescription: The PCM stores P1000-v3 when one or more OBD-II readiness monitors have not completed since the last battery disconnect or code clear. OBD-II monitors have not finished a full readiness drive cycle yet. It is informational, not a hard failure, but the vehicle will not pass an emissions test until the affected monitor sets.
safetyImpact: No safety risk; affects emissions inspection only.

causes.cause: Recent battery disconnect or code clear cleared readiness
Drive cycle conditions not met (temperature, fuel level)
Underlying fault preventing monitor from completing
Failed sensor referenced by the incomplete monitor

symptoms: Readiness flag stays incomplete on scan tool
MIL may flash briefly during diagnostic

fixSteps.title: Check Readiness Status
fixSteps.instruction: Read OBD-II readiness flags with a scan tool to confirm which monitor is incomplete.

fixSteps.title: Drive the Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Perform the manufacturer drive cycle (cold start, mixed driving, steady cruise) with at least 1/4 tank fuel.

fixSteps.title: Resolve Pending Codes
fixSteps.instruction: Repair any other pending DTCs first — they block monitor completion.

fixSteps.title: Verify After Drive
fixSteps.instruction: Re-read readiness flags; all monitors should set after one or two full cycles.

faq.a: Yes — most states require all monitors set before testing.

faq.q: How long is a drive cycle?
faq.a: Typically 20–30 minutes of mixed driving with proper coolant warm-up.

title: MAF Sensor Intermittent (P1100-v4)
shortDescription: Mass airflow sensor signal drops out intermittently during the drive cycle. Stored as P1100-v4.
fullDescription: The PCM stores P1100-v4 when the named fuel/air metering signal is out of expected range or drops out intermittently. Mass airflow sensor signal drops out intermittently during the drive cycle. Diagnose with live data before parts-swapping.
safetyImpact: Reduced power but generally driveable to a shop.

causes.cause: Failed sensor or signal wire
Loose or corroded connector
Vacuum leak skewing readings
Dirty MAF or air filter element
PCM software issue

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Visually check the sensor and connector for damage or contamination.

fixSteps.title: Check Live Data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare sensor reading to expected values across RPM range.

fixSteps.title: Test Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Back-probe sensor connector and verify reference voltage and ground.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install OE sensor and clear codes.

faq.a: Usually not — limp mode may activate but the engine still runs.
Stick with OE for MAF and crank/cam sensors; cheap parts often re-set the same code.

title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1) (P0420-v3)
shortDescription: Bank 1 catalyst is no longer storing enough oxygen to scrub the exhaust. Stored as P0420-v3.
fullDescription: The PCM stores P0420-v3 after comparing upstream and downstream O2 sensors and finding the catalyst no longer scrubs the exhaust effectively. Bank 1 catalyst is no longer storing enough oxygen to scrub the exhaust. A misfire or rich condition can ruin a cat in minutes — fix the underlying cause first.
safetyImpact: No immediate driving danger; emissions degraded.

causes.cause: Aged or damaged catalytic converter
Failing rear (downstream) O2 sensor
Engine misfire damaging the cat
Coolant or oil consumption fouling the substrate
Exhaust leak upstream of the rear sensor

symptoms: Loss of power on hard acceleration

fixSteps.title: Read Live O2 Data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare upstream and downstream O2 traces — downstream should be nearly flat at warm idle.

fixSteps.title: Resolve Misfires First
fixSteps.instruction: Fix any misfire or fuel trim codes before condemning the cat.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for Damage
fixSteps.instruction: Tap the cat — a rattle indicates broken substrate.

fixSteps.title: Replace Catalyst
fixSteps.instruction: Install OE-spec catalytic converter and clear codes.

faq.q: Can I drive with this code?
faq.a: Yes, but emissions are elevated and the cat will degrade further if a misfire is present.

faq.q: Does an aftermarket cat fix it?
faq.a: Universal cats often re-set this code; prefer OE-grade direct-fit converters.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Malfunction (P0440-v3)
shortDescription: Generic EVAP system fault — leak, vent valve, or purge issue. Stored as P0440-v3.
fullDescription: The PCM stores P0440-v3 after running its EVAP self-test and detecting a fault in the sealed evaporative emission system. Generic EVAP system fault — leak, vent valve, or purge issue. Many modern systems use natural-vacuum or pressure-decay methods that need a cool-down soak to run.
safetyImpact: No safety risk; cosmetic and emissions only.

causes.cause: Loose or failed gas cap
Cracked EVAP hose or charcoal canister
Stuck purge or vent solenoid
Leaking fuel tank seal or fuel pump O-ring
Pressure sensor out of range

symptoms: Slight rough idle when purge active

fixSteps.title: Tighten Gas Cap
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten or replace the fuel cap — clear and re-test.

fixSteps.title: Smoke Test EVAP
fixSteps.instruction: Use an EVAP smoke machine to find the leak point.

fixSteps.title: Test Solenoids
fixSteps.instruction: Bi-directional control of purge and vent valves; replace any that don't seal.

fixSteps.title: Replace Faulty Component
fixSteps.instruction: Install new hose / canister / valve; clear codes and run drive cycle.

faq.a: Yes — but fuel vapors escape to atmosphere and you'll fail emissions.
EVAP leaks rarely affect driveability; the test runs only under specific conditions.

EVAP pressure control valve not holding pressure as commanded. Many modern systems use natural-vacuum or pressure-decay methods that need a cool-down soak to run.
safetyImpact: No safety risk; cosmetic and emissions only.

causes.cause: Loose or failed gas cap
Cracked EVAP hose or charcoal canister
Stuck purge or vent solenoid
Leaking fuel tank seal or fuel pump O-ring
Pressure sensor out of range

symptoms: Slight rough idle when purge active

fixSteps.title: Tighten Gas Cap
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten or replace the fuel cap — clear and re-test.

fixSteps.title: Smoke Test EVAP
fixSteps.instruction: Use an EVAP smoke machine to find the leak point.

fixSteps.title: Test Solenoids
fixSteps.instruction: Bi-directional control of purge and vent valves; replace any that don't seal.

fixSteps.title: Replace Faulty Component
fixSteps.instruction: Install new hose / canister / valve; clear codes and run drive cycle.

faq.a: Yes — but fuel vapors escape to atmosphere and you'll fail emissions.
EVAP leaks rarely affect driveability; the test runs only under specific conditions.

title: DEF Tank Temperature Sensor Circuit (P14C0-v2)
shortDescription: Diesel exhaust fluid tank temperature sensor circuit fault. Stored as P14C0-v2.
fullDescription: The PCM (or aftertreatment module) stores P14C0-v2 when it detects a fault in the diesel exhaust fluid heater or temperature circuit on a SCR-equipped vehicle. Diesel exhaust fluid tank temperature sensor circuit fault. Frozen or cold DEF blocks dosing and triggers emission-strategy derates.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may enter limp mode or refuse restart per emissions strategy.

causes.cause: Failed DEF temperature or heater sensor
Damaged DEF tank wiring harness or connector
Failed DEF heater element
Crystallized DEF in lines from contamination
DEF dosing module fault

fixSteps.title: Scan DEF System
fixSteps.instruction: Read DEF tank temperature, heater current, and sensor data.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Check the DEF tank harness for road salt corrosion or chafing.

fixSteps.title: Test Heater Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure heater resistance against spec (typically a few ohms).

fixSteps.title: Replace Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace DEF tank header, sensor, or heater per diagnosis; refill clean DEF.

faq.a: No — most diesels enforce a derate or no-restart within a few hundred miles.
Yes — DEF freezes at -11°C and the system must thaw within minutes of cold start.
